# RGAA mapping

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-rgaa-mapping-doc.js from src/coverage/rgaa-rule-map.js; do not edit by hand. -->

Which RGAA tests each rule checks, and which rules speak to each RGAA criterion. A scan names these tests on its results when asked (`engineOptions.mappings: ['rgaa']`, see [`ENGINE_OPTIONS.md`](./ENGINE_OPTIONS.md#other-standards-mappings)); [`WCAG_CONFORMANCE.md`](./WCAG_CONFORMANCE.md#rgaa) explains how the mapping is made.

> **Review status:** drafted from the RGAA test wording and official methodology, not yet reviewed by an RGAA auditor. [`RGAA_TO_REVIEW.md`](./RGAA_TO_REVIEW.md) lists what still needs checking, by priority. Corrections go in `src/coverage/rgaa-rule-map.js`; this page is regenerated from it.

A rule maps to a test when its failure (or, for a manual rule, the question it raises) is direct evidence about what the test's methodology checks. A mapped rule covers the test in part at most: a `pass` never means an RGAA test is conforme, and most tests need a human. A test marked "(exception)" is linked although RGAA relates it to other WCAG criteria than the rule; the reason follows the note.

## RGAA 4.1.2

113 of 149 rules map to at least one test; they reach 51 of 106 criteria.

| `accesskeys`                               | manual    | —                   | —                                      | Asks for review of duplicate accesskey values across elements. 12.10.1 concerns single-key shortcuts without modifiers, and accesskey always uses a modifier. No RGAA test checks this.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

SVG and MathML content is not checked, where those attributes are geometry rather than presentation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `presentational-children-focusable-absent` | automatic | 4.1.2               | —                                      | Flags tab stops inside roles with presentational children (button, tab, option...). For native button the Nu checker reports interactive content or a tabindex descendant as a nesting error (8.2.1 step 2). Explicit-role cases are mostly not validator errors, and the effect on AT output (7.1.2) is not directly what the rule tests. Not mapped to 8.2.1: the validator 8.2.1 relies on reports only the native-button case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `presentational-elements-absent`           | automatic | —                   | 10.1.1                                 | Fails on each element 10.1.1 step 1 lists (basefont, big, blink, center, font, marquee, s, strike, tt), and on <u> when the doctype is not HTML5 (step 2). Written for RGAA, so it checks exactly that list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `progressbar-name-present`                 | automatic | 1.1.1               | —                                      | Fails an element with explicit role="progressbar" that has no author-supplied name. No image or media test covers it. The closest match is 7.1.1 step 2 (an ARIA/JS component must have an explicit name), but 7.1 is outside the candidate list. Not mapped to 7.1.1: 7.1 is about script-driven components; a missing progressbar name is not what its methodology checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `radio-group-present`                      | manual    | —                   | 11.5.1                                 | Asks about two or more radio buttons with the same name, in the same form, that are not all inside one <fieldset>, role="group" or role="radiogroup", the three ways 11.5.1 accepts. 11.5.1 applies "si nécessaire", so a person decides. Custom role="radio" widgets are not checked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `region`                                   | manual    | —                   | —                                      | Flags content under <body> that is outside any landmark. RGAA does not require all content to be inside landmarks: 12.6.1 accepts alternatives to landmarks for specific zones only, and 9.2.1 covers header/nav/main/footer structure, not leftover content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `role-img-text-alternative-present`        | automatic | 1.1.1               | 1.1.1                                  | Fails an exposed non-<img> element with role="img" (or graphics-symbol/graphics-document) that has no name, which is 1.1.1 step 4. Partial: it also accepts title and SVG <title>, which step 4 does not list, and the graphics-* roles are outside RGAA's wording.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `scope-attr-valid`                         | manual    | —                   | 5.7.2, 8.2.1                           | Flags scope values other than row/col/rowgroup/colgroup. On a th with an invalid scope, 5.7.2 fails because it requires scope="row" or scope="col". An invalid attribute value is also a validity error under 8.2.1. The rule accepts rowgroup/colgroup, so it covers only part of 5.7.2.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `scrollable-region-focusable`              | manual    | 2.1.1, 2.1.3        | —                                      | Flags containers with overflow auto/scroll that have no focusable descendant and are not focusable themselves (keyboard scrolling). No RGAA test covers keyboard scrolling of a plain CSS scroll region: 7.3 needs a script handler, 10.14/12.11 cover extra content shown on hover, focus or activation, and 12.9 covers keyboard traps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `searchbox-name-present`                   | automatic | 4.1.2               | 11.1.1, 7.1.1                          | Checks that role=searchbox has a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or an associated label, matching the conditions in 11.1.1 step 2 for form fields. An unnamed custom searchbox also fails 7.1.1 step 2 (explicit name).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `server-side-image-map-absent`             | automatic | 2.1.1               | 1.1.4 (exception)                      | Fails any <img ismap>, which is exactly step 1 of 1.1.4 (find <img> with ismap). 1.1.4 passes if the page also has links giving the same destinations, which this rule does not check, so a failure is a finding to verify, not an RGAA failure. 1.1 is outside the WCAG-derived candidates, but the element and attribute match exactly. Exception for 1.1.4: RGAA files 1.1.4 under WCAG 1.1.1 and the engine files server-side image maps under 2.1.1 (Keyboard), but the rule and the test look for the same thing: 1.1.4 step 1 finds each <img> with ismap.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `skip-link`                                | manual    | —                   | 12.7.2                                 | Flags 'skip/jump to' links whose #fragment does not resolve to a usable target. This is direct evidence for 12.7.2, where one condition is that the link works ('Le lien est fonctionnel'). The rule does not check the link's position, visibility or consistency across pages, and a skip link can target zones other than main.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `slider-name-present`                      | automatic | 4.1.2               | 11.1.1, 7.1.1                          | Checks that explicit role=slider has a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or an associated label, matching the conditions in 11.1.1 step 2 (slider is an ARIA form-field role). An unnamed custom slider also fails 7.1.1 step 2. Native input[type=range] without the role is out of the rule's scope, despite the rule's description.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `spinbutton-name-present`                  | automatic | 4.1.2               | 11.1.1, 7.1.1                          | Checks that role=spinbutton has a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or an associated label, matching the conditions in 11.1.1 step 2 for form fields. An unnamed custom spinbutton also fails 7.1.1 step 2 (explicit name).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `summary-name-present`                     | automatic | 4.1.2               | —                                      | Flags <summary> elements with an empty name. A native details/summary disclosure is not script-generated, so 7.1.1 does not strictly apply. 11.9.1 covers only buttons inside a form, and no other candidate test concerns disclosure widgets. The auditor may still choose to treat a scripted summary under 7.1.1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `svg-hidden-no-alternative`                | automatic | —                   | 1.1.5, 1.2.4                           | Fails an <svg aria-hidden="true"> that carries a text alternative: aria-label, aria-labelledby, a title attribute, or a non-empty <title> or <desc>. As a decorative image it breaks conditions 2 to 4 of 1.2.4. If the alternative means the image carries information, it is hidden from assistive technology and has no role="img", failing 1.1.5. Which of the two applies needs a human.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `svg-image-text-alternative-present`       | automatic | 1.1.1               | —                                      | Targets SVG <image> child elements. RGAA 1.1.5 covers the <svg> root, and 1.1.1 covers <img> and role="img", so no RGAA test is about naming an inner SVG <image>. It would only matter if that element were given role="img", and role-img-text-alternative-present already covers that case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `svg-text-alternative-present`             | automatic | 1.1.1               | 1.1.5                                  | Fails an <svg> root that seems meant to convey information but has no <title> text and no aria-label/aria-labelledby, which is 1.1.5 step 5. It does not enforce the role="img" requirement of step 3.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `svg-text-alternative-quality`             | manual    | 1.1.1               | 1.3.6                                  | Asks a human to judge the relevance of an <svg>'s existing title/ARIA name, which is 1.3.6 step 2. It also includes desc-only cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `tab-name-present`                         | automatic | 4.1.2               | 7.1.1                                  | Checks that role=tab has a non-empty name. A tab is part of a script-driven tab panel component, and 7.1.1 step 2 requires an explicit name. Not a form field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `tabindex`                                 | manual    | —                   | 12.8.1                                 | Flags positive tabindex values, which override the natural focus order. This is direct evidence for 12.8.1 step 2, whether the tab order stays coherent, though a positive tabindex is not a failure by itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `table-duplicate-name`                     | manual    | —                   | —                                      | Flags tables whose summary attribute repeats the caption. For a complex data table, a summary that only repeats the title does not explain the table's structure, which bears on 5.2.1 (is the summary relevant). It does not apply to simple tables. Not mapped to 5.2.1: 5.2.1 concerns the summary of complex tables only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `table-fake-caption`                       | manual    | 1.3.1               | 5.4.1                                  | Flags tables with no <caption> whose first row is a single cell above multi-cell rows, asking whether that cell is a visual title not tied to the table. That is 5.4.1 step 2: is the data table's title given by caption, title, aria-label or aria-labelledby? The rule does not check title or aria-label, so the reviewer should look for those.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `table-headers-attr-valid`                 | automatic | 1.3.1               | 5.7.4, 8.2.1 (exception)               | Fails a td/th whose headers attribute references an id that is missing, points to a non-cell, points to the cell itself, or sits in another table, so headers does not list the ids of the associated headers (5.7.4 step 2, second condition). Such references are also flagged by the Nu checker (8.2.1, secondary). Exception for 8.2.1: RGAA relates 8.2 to WCAG 4.1.1 and 4.1.2; the engine files this rule under another criterion because WCAG 2.2 removed 4.1.1 (Parsing). A headers attribute that names no cell of the table is an invalid attribute value under 8.2.1, which the validator reports.                                                                                                                                                |
| `table-th-has-data-cells`                  | automatic | 1.3.1               | —                                      | Fails a table (not role=presentation) that has <th> but no <td> at all. If the auditor judges it a layout table, the <th> use fails 5.8.1 step 2. If it is a data table whose cells are all marked <th>, no RGAA test forbids that (5.6.4 allows th), so the auditor must decide which applies. Not mapped to 5.8.1: only a failure if the auditor judges the table a layout table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `target-size-minimum`                      | automatic | 2.5.8               | —                                      | Checks the 24x24 CSS px target size and spacing exception of WCAG 2.5.8, a WCAG 2.2 criterion RGAA 4.1.2 does not include. No RGAA test measures pointer target size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `td-has-header`                            | automatic | 1.3.1               | 5.6.1, 5.6.2                           | In large tables (4x4 or more, no colspan/rowspan), fails a <td> with no headers attribute and no <th> above it in its column or before it in its row. This is strong evidence that the column or row headers are not declared as <th> (5.6.1 and 5.6.2 step 2). It does not check the association technique (5.7), and it ignores role=columnheader/rowheader, which 5.6 accepts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `textbox-name-present`                     | automatic | 4.1.2               | 11.1.1, 7.1.1                          | Checks that role=textbox has a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or an associated label, matching the conditions in 11.1.1 step 2 for form fields. An unnamed custom textbox also fails 7.1.1 step 2 (explicit name).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tooltip-name-present`                     | automatic | 4.1.2               | —                                      | Flags role=tooltip with an empty name, which in practice means an empty tooltip. A tooltip is supplementary content, not an operable component whose name 7.1.1 step 2 evaluates. None of the candidate tests checks tooltip content, so a fit to 7.1.1 would be weak.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `treeitem-name-present`                    | automatic | 4.1.2               | 7.1.1                                  | Checks that role=treeitem has a non-empty name. A tree item is part of a script-driven tree component, and 7.1.1 step 2 requires an explicit name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `valid-lang`                               | automatic | 3.1.2               | 8.8.1                                  | Checks that lang on elements other than <html> is a syntactically valid language tag. That is the 'valide' condition of 8.8.1 for language changes; relevance is not checked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `video-caption`                            | manual    | 1.2.2               | 4.3.1                                  | Flags <video> without a <track kind=captions\|subtitles>, raising the question of 4.3.1 step 2 (are synchronised captions present?). It accepts kind="subtitles", so it gives no evidence for 4.3.2 (kind="captions" required).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `video-captions-track-kind`                | automatic | —                   | 4.3.2                                  | Fails a <video> whose subtitle tracks are all kind="subtitles" (or have no kind, which means subtitles), with none kind="captions". That is 4.3.2 as written. Whether the video is pre-recorded synchronised media, and whether a track carries captions at all, needs a human.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `video-poster-text-alternative-present`    | automatic | 1.1.1               | —                                      | Checks that a <video poster> has an accessible name. No RGAA 4.1.2 test targets poster images: the theme-1 tests list img/area/input/svg/object/embed/canvas, and the theme-4 tests are about transcripts, captions and AT compatibility of the media player, not naming a <video>.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| **1.1** Chaque image porteuse d’information a-t-elle une alternative textuelle ?                                                                                                                             | 1.1.1: `img-alt-decorative`, `img-alt-present`, `role-img-text-alternative-present`<br>1.1.2: `area-alt-present`<br>1.1.3: `input-image-alt-present`<br>1.1.4: `server-side-image-map-absent`<br>1.1.5: `img-alt-decorative`, `svg-hidden-no-alternative`, `svg-text-alternative-present`<br>1.1.6: `object-text-alternative-present`<br>1.1.7: `embed-text-alternative-present`<br>1.1.8: `canvas-text-alternative-present`, `img-alt-decorative` |

| **1.6** Chaque image porteuse d’information a-t-elle, si nécessaire, une description détaillée ?                                                                                                             | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
